name: Echinacea
short: In trials, adverse events were no more common than with controls. A safety review found rare allergic reactions that may be severe and urged care in people with allergy or asthma.
text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 48 clinical studies (10,115 participants) of oral echinacea found adverse events were slightly less frequent with echinacea than with controls, and serious adverse events were very rare with no deaths. A Cochrane review of 24 trials likewise found no significant difference in dropouts or reported adverse effects, though in prevention trials there was a trend towards more people stopping echinacea because of adverse events. An earlier systematic safety review, which also drew on spontaneous reports, found that gastrointestinal upsets and rashes occur most frequently and that in rare cases echinacea can be associated with allergic reactions that may be severe; it advised people with allergy or asthma to consider their use carefully and judged use in pregnancy and breastfeeding ill-advised because data are sparse. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
